findings.claim: The DELETE handler in app/api/listings/[id]/route.ts is left without any session or role check, so any unauthenticated caller can delete listings.
findings.evidence: `DELETE /api/listings/[id]` — unchanged; it already validates the id is a UUID and returns 404 when the listing does not exist, which is enough.
findings.recommendation: Call getSession() and require role = 'admin' before deleting.

findings.claim: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY ships the Supabase service-role key to the browser bundle because NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are inlined into client code.
findings.evidence: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=...   # needed by the admin pages, which run client-side
findings.recommendation: Keep the service-role key server-only and route bulk edits through an admin API.

findings.claim: The callback route performs an open redirect: it redirects to the unvalidated `next` query parameter, which a phishing link can point at an attacker domain.
findings.recommendation: Only allow relative same-origin paths for next.

findings.claim: POST /api/auth/request-link has no rate limit, so an attacker can flood arbitrary inboxes with login emails.
findings.evidence: Always return `202` regardless of whether the email exists
findings.recommendation: Rate limit by IP and by email address.
